description: Reference scenario s3-after-the-session (twin) on the synthetic student of fixtures/students/maya: "Update my follow-ups from yesterday". Load with env.load_seed at virtual_now 2027-03-01T09:00:00-05:00 with this binding.json, then apply the twin setup in ../scenario.json.

sources.description: Hand-written synthetic centre, tutors, timetable, student, accommodations, appointments, intakes, reports and follow-ups (fixtures/centre.json and fixtures/profiles/maya.json). The centre settings and intake fields follow the common pattern of public university tutoring and writing-centre policies, in my own words. The student, the tutors, the centre and its school are fictional. No external collection and no third-party text.

The 40 Algebra 1 and Introductory Statistics skill IDs and titles are those of Milepost's course catalog (apps/milepost/fixtures/catalog/courses.json, PR #70, same author, MIT), so a task can load both Apps for the same student. Milepost wrote those titles in its own words after the section structure of two OpenStax textbooks; no textbook text is reproduced here.

Records written by hand for the scenario (examples/scenarios/s3-after-the-session/scenario.json). Both members: None: the full fixture as it is. The setup records Tuesday's writing session with Sam as completed and posts his report: revise the lab report's thesis by Thursday 17:00 (fu-9, kind revise) and read the centre's guide on evidence (fu-10, kind read). An older reading from January (fu-3) is still open. Twin only: Sam's first follow-up asks Maya to read his comments on the thesis by Thursday (kind read, bio-lab-3-comments, 15 minutes) instead of revising it.

transformations: The centre timetable expanded into 50-minute slots for the two weeks of slot_window, with past slots added for the history; slot IDs are the tutor, the local date and the local start time (ana-0304-0800).
Times written in America/New_York with their UTC offset.
Scenario changes applied to the full fixture maya, then the twin changes.

review.notes: Automated checks do not replace the author's check of every record and human review of realism and variation.
